$comment: Every asset this project downloads, in one place. `npm run download-assets`
reads this file and nothing else, so an asset that is not listed here is not
reproducible and should not be relied on.
NOTHING FROM A RETAIL QUAKE III INSTALL BELONGS IN THIS FILE. Commercial Q3
content is not redistributable and is not downloadable; it is sourced from the
user's own installation via tools/build-devpak.ts. See NOTICE.
`sha256` is recorded on first successful download so later runs can detect a
changed upstream. A null sha means 'not yet pinned' -- the download will
succeed and print the hash to paste back in.
An entry with `manual` cannot be fetched by a script (a JS bot challenge, a
click-through). The tool prints instructions instead of pretending otherwise,
and still runs `extract` if the file has been placed by hand.

downloads.name: openarena-pak0
downloads.description: OpenArena 0.8.8 baseoa/pak0.pk3. Third-party MD3 models and textures for the asset tests.
$note: 38MB, 150 .md3 files, and player models grism/sarge/sorceress.
This is what makes test/assets/md3.test.ts run on a clean checkout: a
writer and a parser built from the same struct definitions agree with
each other even when both are wrong, so only third-party files settle
the on-disk layout.
The SourceForge /download URL redirects to a mirror with an expiring
token, so the stable /download form is what belongs here -- never the
resolved master.dl.sourceforge.net link.

downloads.description: OpenArena base_floor/achtung_clang.jpg. One of the five images ob_basics needs; see $note on the first of them.
downloads.license: GPLv2 (OpenArena). Freely redistributable, and unlike retail Quake III content it MAY be committed. See NOTICE.
$note: ob_basics is the tutorial course, and it is the one map that has to work
on a clean clone with no Quake III installation -- a first map that needs
commercial assets is not a first map. It was retextured onto OpenArena
names for exactly that reason.
It references eight shaders; three are common/ nodraw and never render, so
these five images plus scripts/oasky.shader are the whole requirement.
The shader is already inside oa-pak0.pk3 above -- only the images were
missing from it, because that download is a libsdl-android build carrying
models and sounds and no map texture sets at all.
Individual files rather than an OpenArena texture pak: 262KB against a
hundred megabytes, and each one carries its own hash.
`npm run build-oapak` zips these into public/ob_basics.pk3.

downloads.manual: ws.q3df.org sits behind a Cloudflare JS challenge, which returns 403 to any scripted client. Open the URL in a browser, then save the .pk3 to the path below and re-run this command.
$note: Get this map from q3df, NOT from the copy that ships in some Quake III
installations. The competition build wraps its .bsp in an 'EZPZ'
container so only the organisers' client will open it -- the file is
intact and the .pk3 unzips fine, it simply is not a BSP. Stock Quake III
rejects it too: CM_LoadMap checks the version field and that build
reports 48 where Quake III wants 46.
`parseBsp` recognises the EZPZ ident and says so by name rather than
failing with a hex number. Unwrapping it is deliberately not
implemented: the wrapper exists to control which clients can read the
map, and the maps are published unprotected afterwards anyway.

Unlike the game-content downloads in this manifest, font files ARE

needs them to render correctly on a clean clone with no network access
and no player-supplied .pk3 mounted yet. `public/fonts/` is therefore
NOT gitignored, unlike the rest of public/. Re-run this command only to
refresh from upstream; the checked-in files are what ships.

$note: One file, a variable font -- `font-weight: 400 700` in the @font-face
rule lets the browser interpolate 500 rather than needing a fourth
static file. See font-barlow-condensed-regular's note on why this is
committed rather than gitignored like the rest of public/.
`dest` renames upstream's `JetBrainsMono[wght].ttf` -- square brackets
are both a glob metacharacter and Rollup's output-placeholder syntax
([name], [hash]), and `vite build` processes this file's @font-face
url() and index.html's <link> for it. There is no reason to keep
upstream's filename; `dest` is this project's to choose.
